title: Forever No. 1: Shelley Fabares, ‘Johnny Angel’
summary: When she dethroned Connie Francis, it marked the first time female singers had back-to-back No. 1s on the Hot 100.
body: Forever No. 1 is a Billboard series that pays special tribute to the recently deceased artists who achieved the highest honor our charts have to offer — a Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 single — by taking an extended look back at the chart-topping songs that made them part of this exclusive club. Here, we honor the late TV star Shelley Fabares, whose “Johnny Angel” reached No. 1 in April 1962. “Johnny Angel” is so innocent, so chaste, that it immediately conjures a simpler time. It has that in common with such other defining hits of the era as The Chordettes’ “Mr. Sandman” (1954) and The Teddy Bears’ “To Know Him, Is To Love Him” (1958). “Johnny Angel” is a classic “crush” song, in which the singer pines about a boy who is utterly oblivious:”Johnny Angel, how I love him/ He’s got something that I can’t resist/ But he doesn’t even know that I exist.” Related Gone But Not Forgotten: Musicians We Lost in 2026 Forever No. 1: Connie Francis, ‘My Heart Has a Mind of Its Own’ Forever No. 1: Connie Francis’ ‘Everybody’s Somebody’s Fool’ Singer and actress Shelley Fabares , who died on Sunday (Aug. 23) in Los Angeles at a…

title: KATSEYE, Phoebe Bridgers, Ella Langley & More: Highlights of This Week’s Billboard Charts
summary: All of Billboard’s charts update each Tuesday.
body: Tuesday is new Billboard chart day each week! As all charts update each Tuesday morning, here’s a look at highlights of the latest rankings, dated Aug. 29 and reflecting the Aug. 14-20 measurement week, according to data tracker Luminate. Among this week’s chart stars are KATSEYE , Phoebe Bridgers, Ella Langley, Taylor Swift and Karol G. KATSEYE earns its first No. 1 on the  Billboard 200  as  WILD  debuts with 170,000 equivalent album units in the United States in its first week, ending Aug. 20, according to Luminate. “EYEKONS, this is so surreal!!,” the group posted in celebration. “Thank you for showing  WILD  so much love.” KATSEYE also tops the Billboard Artist 100 for the first time, vaulting from No. 28 and passing its prior No. 6 peak. Plus, the group debuts at No. 31 on the Billboard Hot 100 with the EP’s latest single, “Hootie Frutti.” The act adds its sixth top 40 hit on the chart, all earned consecutively and all of which have peaked this year. The song joins “Gabriella” (No. 21), “Internet Girl” (No. 29, both in January), “Pinky Up” (No. 28, April), star team-up “Iconic by Mistake,” with LE SSERAFIM and ILLIT (No. 38, June), an…

title: Is Digi-Pop the Newest Hyperpop Wave?
summary: How Pupsies' debut chart hit "Misery" could be leading the charge.
body: What’s initially most striking about Pupsies’ “Misery” is the song’s sonics: a buzzing, blaring, synth-bass hum matched with a lo-fi melody that could soundtrack an 8-bit video game. While Pupsies’ favorite part kicks in later — a dramatic, crunchy guitar hook from co-producer Goetia that accompanies her wailing vocal climax — it’s this early, beatless section that helped the song take off on TikTok. Cindy Kamgaing, the 19-year-old from North Carolina better known as Pupsies, has been building an internet following since 2023 for her kinetic, therapeutically revealing digi-pop jams, but had yet to really unlock a mainstream crossover until “Misery.” Following its March release, the emotionally overflowing (but “cute”-­sounding, as Kamgaing proudly puts it) single went viral, taking off with animation edits (like a Steven Universe one that Kamgaing found particularly delightful), and with users jokingly referring to it as a “LARP” song (an abbreviation that traditionally means live action role playing but has come to refer to anyone seen as playing a specific part). “I think people started saying it because the song is kind of like, ‘I’m depressed, I’m a girl,’” Kamgaing says. The animation has been tinted to simulate what a human would see if they were watching the transit from the Martian surface through protective solar eclipse glasses. Perseverance has captured several Phobos transits since its landing at Jezero Crater in February 2021. By comparing the various recordings, scientists can refine their understanding of the potato-shaped moon’’ orbit, learning how it is changing.
